20261122-chemistry-g03-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Thought Experiment] Does air, which cannot be seen, also have weight (mass), like a solid or a liquid? What is the most valid experimental method to prove this?

20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.prompt: A cold drink can just taken out of the refrigerator was left on the table for a while, and droplets of water formed on the surface of the can. Where did these droplets come from?
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.explain: This is 'condensation (liquefaction),' in which water vapor in the air, in a gaseous state, meets the cold surface of the can, loses heat, and changes into liquid water droplets.
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.hint.0: Invisible water vapor is always floating in the air.
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.hint.1: When water vapor meets a cold surface, it cools and turns into liquid droplets (condensation).
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.o.o0: Water vapor, a gas in the air, touched the cold can and condensed into liquid water
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.o.o1: The drink leaked out through the aluminum wall of the can
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.o.o2: Droplets formed from the paint on the can surface melting
20261118-chemistry-g04.s.s1.o.o3: Sap squeezed out of the wood of the table

20261121-chemistry-g04-2.material: Which statement correctly explains the difference between 'evaporation' and 'boiling' that occur when water is heated in a pot?

20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.prompt: Which statement correctly explains the difference between 'evaporation' and 'boiling' that occur when water is heated in a pot?
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.explain: Evaporation is the phenomenon in which molecules at the liquid surface vaporize even at temperatures below the boiling point, and boiling is the phenomenon in which, on reaching the boiling point, vaporization occurs actively not only at the surface but throughout the interior of the liquid.
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.hint.0: Laundry drying is evaporation, which happens slowly at the surface even at low temperatures.
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.hint.1: Water boiling vigorously is boiling, with bubbles bursting from inside at 100 degrees.
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o0: Evaporation occurs only at the surface of a liquid, while boiling occurs at the boiling point (100℃) with bubbles forming at the surface and throughout the interior of the liquid
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o1: Evaporation occurs only at 100℃, and boiling occurs at all temperatures
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o2: Evaporation is water turning into ice, and boiling is water turning into water vapor
20261121-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o3: Evaporation and boiling are exactly the same phenomenon

20261122-chemistry-g04-1.title: Advanced Change of State
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.goal: អនុវត្តគោលការណ៍នៃ Advanced Change of State ដើម្បីដោះស្រាយបញ្ហាស្រាវជ្រាវ។
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.material: [Advanced Change of State] Water in a beaker was heated until it began to boil vigorously. Why does the thermometer reading stop rising above 100℃ even if the flame is made stronger and heat continues to be applied?
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.thinking.1: ការវែកញែកសមហេតុផលនិងការវិភាគ
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Change of State] Water in a beaker was heated until it began to boil vigorously. Why does the thermometer reading stop rising above 100℃ even if the flame is made stronger and heat continues to be applied?
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.explain: While a pure liquid boils, the heat energy applied is used up entirely in breaking the attractions between molecules and converting them to the gaseous state (heat of vaporization), so the temperature stays constant until all of the water has turned into water vapor.
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.hint.0: While matter changes state, its temperature stays constant.
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.hint.1: This is called 'latent heat (heat of vaporization).'
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.o.o0: Because the supplied heat energy is used entirely for the change of state of water into water vapor (heat of vaporization) instead of raising the temperature of the water
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.o.o1: Because the thermometer breaks above 100 degrees
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.o.o2: Because the water can no longer absorb heat
20261122-chemistry-g04-1.s.s1.o.o3: Because the water vapor cools the thermometer

20261122-chemistry-g04-2.title: Which option correctly pairs the

20261122-chemistry-g04-2.material: Which option correctly pairs the change-of-state processes of the clear 'dew' that forms on blades of grass in the early morning and the white 'frost' that forms on windows and roofs on late-autumn nights?
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.thinking.1: ការវែកញែកសមហេតុផលនិងការវិភាគ
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.prompt: Which option correctly pairs the change-of-state processes of the clear 'dew' that forms on blades of grass in the early morning and the white 'frost' that forms on windows and roofs on late-autumn nights?
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.explain: Dew is water vapor in the air condensing (liquefying) on the surface of grass blades chilled overnight, and frost is deposition (solidifying sublimation), in which water vapor at sub-zero temperatures turns directly into ice crystals without passing through a liquid.
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.hint.0: Dew is liquid water droplets (water vapor → liquid).
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.hint.1: Frost is ice crystals that form at sub-zero temperatures (water vapor → solid).
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o0: Dew: water vapor turns into liquid droplets (liquefaction) / Frost: water vapor turns directly into ice crystals (sublimation)
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o1: Dew: ice melts (melting) / Frost: water boils (vaporization)
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o2: Both dew and frost are water that evaporated into water vapor
20261122-chemistry-g04-2.s.s1.o.o3: Dew: spring water that welled up from the ground / Frost: snow that fell from the sky
